S&P 500 gave up yesterday's gains ending the week with solid red candle. However, the premiums for SPX contracts were still pricy compare to the volatility. I tested the call side and it failed right away so scalped a put position, ending flat for the day (never go against the trend; especially intraday when it is consistently heading lower as it tests the lower band VWAP). I expect this volatility to continue into next week but hopefully the premiums will come down a bit, presenting better opportunities. Happy Friday!

“You cannot step into the same river twice.” This is a profound insight into the nature of life, discovered 2,500 years ago by the Greek philosopher Heraclitus. Look at a river. On the surface, it always appears the same, but the river from one second ago is completely different from the river now. Life is the same way. The person I was yesterday is not the same person I am today. Our thoughts, emotions, and even our cells change every moment. Strictly speaking, the person you were one second ago is different from who you are now. Heraclitus said, “The only constant is change.” Even the things we believe are unchanging; our personalities, abilities, and destinies are actually constantly flowing. This realization brings comfort. Just because life is difficult now doesn't mean it will be difficult forever. Failure, loss, and disappointment all flow away like a river. But on the other hand, today's success and good fortune will not last forever either. That is why he teaches us, “Do not fear change. Embrace it.” That is the essence of life. Life is not a still river, but a flowing one. So instead of trying to hold on, live in the present moment and move with the flow. You become a new person every moment. And just like a flowing river, your life continues to move forward.

Rich people don't say this. Money doesn't make you happier, but not having it makes you miserable. True wealth isn't money; it's freedom. Being able to avoid things you don't want to do or people you don't want to see. That's the true wealth. The rich earn through investments, while the poor earn through labor. Don't sell your time; build a system, buy in increments of 100 shares to sell covered calls. Make your money work while you sleep. That's how the rich think. Saving is training to control your desires. The person who can endure now owns the future. Building assets is a habit, not spending. The habit of investing $10 a day is worth more than a designer item. Money is a tool. Without character, it becomes a weapon. Money doesn't change people; it reveals their true nature. And remember, the value of time is more important than money. You can make money again, but time doesn't come back. From today, chase freedom, not money because that's the real path of the "rich".

A good decision doesn't always lead to a good outcome. A bad decision can succeed by luck. We judge decisions by their outcomes, but that is the most dangerous illusion. As poker champion Annie Duke says, "Life isn't chess, it's poker." Not all information is visible. So decisions should be evaluated based on the information and process at the time, not the result. A failed trade/startup could still have been a good decision if it was the best choice given what you knew. Winning the lottery isn't a good decision, it's luck. There is no such thing as a perfect decision. Only 1 thing matters: did you choose the option with the highest probability? Don't be swayed by outcomes. If the process was sound, that decision is already a success.

If you improve by just 1% each day, in a year, you'll be 37 times better. It's a miracle proven by math. The British cycling team had never won in a hundred years. But at the 2008 Olympics, they swept 8 gold medals. The secret? Improving by 0.1%. They reduced the weight of the bike by 0.1%, and adjusted posture by 0.1%. James Clear said, "Improving 1% a day makes you 37 times better in a year. Declining 1% a day gets you close to zero." The power of compounding applies to habits too. Read one page a day, that's 365 pages in a year. Learn one new thing a day, that's 365 new knowledge in a year. Add one push-up a day, and your body will change in a year. People want big changes, but real change grows where it's not visible. A bamboo tree grows only three meters in five years, but in the sixth year, it grows 30 meters in just six weeks. That's because it spent five years growing roots. Start today. Improve by just 0.1%. Wake up 10 minutes earlier, drink an extra glass of water, climb one more flight of stairs. Don't dismiss it as too small. That's the power of compounding. Those small changes add up and change your life.

A 13-year-old girl lost her arm to a shark while surfing. As soon as she regained consciousness, she asked, "When can I surf again?" Her name is Bethany Hamilton. In 2003, in the waters of Hawaii, a shark bit off her entire left arm. With the sea stained with blood, no one believed she would get back up. But just three weeks later, she went back out to the ocean. People said it was impossible with one arm. On her first day back, she was thrown around and wiped out 26 times. Still, she didn't stop. "Surfing is my everything. I won't give up." A year after the accident, she won a national competition. She beat surfers with two arms. And she said, "I don't hate the shark. This made me stronger." People asked, "How did you start again?" She answered with a smile, "I wasn't afraid of living without an arm. I was afraid of living without a dream." Is the dream you're about to give up really more important than an arm? Today, Bethany still rides the waves with one arm. There's no reason to give up. Just start.

I entered a long position last night; I moved my stop up to couple points above break even to secure profit when the overnight S&P 500 futures started to climb. This morning when the Michigan consumer sentiment report and Michigan expected inflation report came out, market pulled back towards the support (lower band VWAP, refer to SPY chart 1st image on options), which made my position to hit my stop. Scalped some long positions on the way up but did not feel confident to hold after that choppy overnight move. No short sides were traded towards EOD.

22pts; 16 round turns

Today, SPY tested lower band VWAP (yellow line on 1st attached image) after rejecting the VWAP (purple line on 1st attached image) at open. Lower band VWAP turned out to be the support zone and price started to increase beyond VWAP (open level). After the price surpassed VWAP, I entered SPX 7810Cs, anticipating a breakout above upper band VWAP (pink line on 1st attached image), (SPY chart; SPX chart lacks volume statistic indicators like VWAP). However, the breakout wasn't strong enough for me to hold. After 7810Cs chopped between VWAP and upper band VWAP. I re-entered 7810Cs again expecting that it would surpass the upper band VWAP on this double bottom. However, 7810Cs made a third pull back before a breakout, making me exit the position for breakeven before the big breakout. No put side was traded today during the reversal towards EOD.

It is so important to show up every market day and learn to stare at the chart without taking a trade. I can’t emphasize enough how important it is to show up. As full time traders, we are just merely managing the risk of our portfolio everyday. In the market everyone is competing against Warren Buffett to hedge fund managers to private traders like us who sits in front of our computer literally +80hours weekly staring at the tape/thinking about the market even though actual trades/scalps take minutes. It’s important to comprehend that 95% lose money in the market and among those profitable 5%, 99% are active traders, meaning they trade almost everyday. “Trading is hard” is an understatement because most will lose everything and there’s no guarantee you will be profitable in the future. Real traders would understand how much the market breaks you; your ego, your illusions of control, your sense of certainty and tests your worst. How you question yourself, your process, and your future more times than you want to admit. However, if you are a trader you will come back and show up for the market everyday. You really got to love it and that’s what defines a trader. There is an ancient Arabic saying: a group of sheep led by one lion will beat a group of lions led by one sheep. Become a lion in the market.

Frustrating day as my positions were hitting stops every time I moved it down for a point or two to secure profit. Gave up what I recovered during the morning scalps from those little chops, ended the day back at -30pts. Definitely overtraded today.
